claim.supported_scope: Binary logistic maximum-likelihood regression with an intercept, exact numeric 0/1 complete-case outcomes, numeric predictors and controls, deterministic Newton-IRLS, fixed two-sided 95 percent Wald inference, odds ratios, probabilities, classification diagnostics, and likelihood fit statistics.
claim.estimand: Conditional log odds and odds ratios for a binary outcome under the bounded unpenalized logistic model.
assumptions: Outcome observations are independent and contain both exact numeric classes 0 and 1 after complete-case filtering.
The declared numeric design is full rank and has no detected complete separation or extreme fitted-probability instability.
Model-based inverse-information Wald inference is appropriate for the declared analysis.
exclusions: Multinomial and ordinal outcomes, automatic categorical encoding, survey or case weights, clustered covariance, and mixed models are excluded.
Firth, penalized, robust-covariance, bootstrap, and custom confidence-level inference are excluded.
Classification diagnostics are in-sample descriptions and are not predictive-validation estimates.
warnings: Wald inference can be unreliable with small samples, sparse outcomes, separation, or severe scaling problems.
The fixed 0.5 classification threshold is descriptive and must not be presented as an optimized decision rule.

equations.expression: beta_next = beta + inverse(X_prime W X) X_prime (y - p)

references.citation: Nelder and Wedderburn (1972), Generalized Linear Models
Independent Python and external-R arithmetic comparison for the frozen logistic v2 contract

simulations.design: Preregistered full-rank binary-outcome designs spanning balanced and imbalanced prevalence and bounded coefficient magnitudes.
simulations.seed_policy: Frozen indexed data-generation streams; estimation itself is deterministic.
simulations.acceptance_rule: The dedicated simulation report must meet its frozen bias, coverage, convergence, and failure boundaries without discarding failed fits.

simulations.design: Exact non-binary, single-class, rank-deficient, completely separated, and extreme-probability boundary fixtures.
simulations.seed_policy: Deterministic named fixtures with no random estimation path.
simulations.acceptance_rule: Every unsupported fixture must be rejected with the specified diagnostic and zero committed partial results.

boundaries.case: The complete-case outcome is non-binary or single-class, or the numeric design is rank deficient or separated.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Execution fails with a typed diagnostic and no completed logistic payload.

boundaries.case: The recipe requests multinomial, ordinal, weighted, penalized, or clustered logistic estimation.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Setup is blocked before execution and identifies the unsupported option.

boundaries.case: Predictors and controls are consistently reordered with their identities preserved.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Mapped coefficient and fit results remain equal within the frozen tolerance.

boundaries.case: The same recipe and dataset are executed repeatedly.
boundaries.expected_behavior: All analytical payload fields are exactly equal apart from operational timestamps.

boundaries.case: A coefficient, probability, fit statistic, outcome profile, method identity, or source fingerprint is altered after execution.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Strict archive validation rejects the entire changed result.

tamper_tests.expected_behavior: Reject a result whose capability identity differs from its recipe.
Reject a result relabeled as another logistic method version.
Reject a result whose saved dataset fingerprint no longer matches.
Reject any modified archive entry whose checksum no longer matches.
Reject duplicated keys, unknown fields, non-finite values, invalid counts, or inconsistent arithmetic.
Never reinterpret regression_logistic_v1 output as a current v2 result.

persistence.legacy_policy: Historical regression_logistic_v1 payloads remain readable but cannot be appended or promoted as logistic v2 evidence.

native.gui_cli_parity_rule: For the same dataset and recipe, GUI and CLI analytical payloads must be exactly equal apart from operational timestamps.
accessibility_rules: Every coefficient, fit, and classification visualization has an equivalent accessible table.
Warnings and failure diagnostics are available without color or pointer interaction.
